newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS-China stocks plummet on state bank fund ban.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-China stocks plummet on state bank fund ban.

text.p: China's A and B share indices plummeted on Friday after Beijing stepped up its drive against speculative trading with new measures banning state bank funds from entering the stock markets, brokers said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index lost 3.869 points or 4.34 percent to close at 85.337 points on trading volume of $18.6 million, compared to $9.53 million on Thursday.
The Shenzhen B share market plunged 6.00 points or 3.83 percent to close at 150.77, with turnover hitting HK$87 million against Thursday's HK$48 million.

The People's Bank of China, the central bank, announced the ban late on Thursday, ordering state banks to offset their existing stock positions within 10 days and to stop trading on the state debt repo market from Friday.
"The market will need about two weeks to digest the news but I doubt it will soon return to recent highs," said one analyst with Jardine Fleming Securities in Shenzhen.

Analysts said the Shenzhen B index could lose five percent to 10 percent in the near future while traders in Shanghai said that city's B index could fall another five percent to eight percent next week before stabilising.
"The B share market will be hit less hard by the crackdown because it has not gained as much recently as its A share counterpart," said one analyst at J&A Securities.
Shanghai's A share index ended down 89.498 points or 6.3 percent to 1,331.937 points on turnover of 12.9 billion yuan against 9.1 billion yuan on Thursday.
Shenzhen's A index dived 32.28 points or 6.83 percent to 440.21 on turnover of 12.7 billion yuan, compared to 7.3 billion yuan on Thursday.
Traders predicted further falls on the A share markets of about 15 percent next week.

Brokers said state banks accounted for about 50 percent of liquidity on the state debt repurchase market, which has served as a fund reservoir for the A share markets on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges.
"By drying up the bank funds, liquidity on both the stock markets and the debt markets will fall significantly," an analyst at PBI Securities said.
"The indices still have the potential to fall because money is expected to flow out of the market," said one trader.
On Shenzhen's B share market, Guangdong Province Expressway Co Ltd was the sharpest loser, falling 0.62 points or 8.16 percent to HK$6.98.
Wafangdian Bearing Co bucked the trend and rose HK$0.11 or 2.05 percent to HK$5.47.
In Shanghai, Shanghai Post and Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd was the worst B share performer, losing $0.05 to close at its 10 percent limit-down level of $0.45.
Many A share also companies hit their 10-percent limit-down level.
